'''''Avellinia''''' is a [[genus]] of [[Mediterranean]] plants in the [[Poaceae|grass family]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delta-intkey.com/grass/www/avellini.htm |title=The grass genera of the world: descriptions, illustrations, identification, and information retrieval; including synonyms, morphology, anatomy, physiology, phytochemistry, cytology, classification, pathogens, world and local distribution, and references |accessdate=2009-08-19 |author=Watson L, Dallwitz MJ. |date=2008 |work=The Grass Genera of the World |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114213220/http://delta-intkey.com/grass/www/avellini.htm |archivedate=2007-11-14 }}</ref><ref>Parlatore, Filippo, 1842. Plantae Novae vel minus notae opusculis diversis olim descriptae, page 59</ref><ref>Cabi, E. & M. Doğan. 2012. Poaceae. 690–756. In A. Güner, S. Aslan, T. Ekim, M. Vural & M. T. Babaç (eds.) Türkiye Bitkileri Listesi. Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanik Bahçesi ve Flora Araştırmaları Derneği Yayını, Istanbul</ref> The only known species is '''''Avellinia festucoides''''', found throughout much of the [[Mediterranean Region]] from [[Portugal]] and [[Morocco]] to [[Turkey]].<ref name=u>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=450729 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.3372/wi.36.36202|page=662|title=The Euro+Med treatment of ''Gramineae'' — a generic synopsis and some new names |year=2006 |last1=Valdés |first1=Benito |last2=Scholz |first2=Hildemar |journal=Willdenowia |volume=36 |issue=2 |s2cid=86239547 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Avellinia Altervista Flora Italiana, genere ''Avellinia'']</ref>  It is also reportedly naturalized in [[Australia]].<ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:348448# Atlas of Living Australia]</ref>

The type species is ''Avellinia michelii'' <small>(Savi) Parl.</small><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40023219 Tropicos, Avellinia Parl.]</ref>
